questions.q: In the lab scenario, why does the new VM belong in the internal 10.20.1.0/24 subnet rather than the public-facing one?
options: It has no reason to be reachable from the internet, so it has no reason to sit in a subnet routed for that
Azure requires all VMs to be created in the lowest-numbered subnet available
The public subnet was already full and had no IP addresses left
Subnet placement has no effect on which traffic can reach a VM
questions.explain: Placing a VM in the subnet that matches its actual exposure need is most of the network design decision already made.

questions.q: Why is the SSH key pair generated before the VM is even created?
options: So the public key can be installed on the VM at boot, removing the need for password authentication entirely
Because Azure requires a key pair to exist before it will assign a region
So the key can be emailed to the VM's operating system vendor for approval
Key pairs are optional and only affect font rendering in the terminal
questions.explain: The public key is installed when the VM is provisioned, so password login for SSH never needs to be enabled at all.

questions.q: Why is the NSG's inbound rule for port 22 scoped to Briarcliff's office IP range instead of 0.0.0.0/0?
options: Opening SSH to the entire internet invites automated login attempts almost immediately; scoping the source narrows who can even attempt a connection
0.0.0.0/0 is not valid syntax in a network security group rule
Port 22 must always be restricted to a single IP address, never a range
Scoping the rule has no real security benefit, only a cosmetic one
questions.explain: A rule scoped to a known source range is far harder to abuse than one that accepts SSH attempts from anywhere.

questions.q: What does running systemctl status sshd confirm that simply knowing port 22 is open does not?
options: That the SSH service itself is actually active and able to accept sessions, not just that the port is theoretically reachable
That the VM has been patched with the latest security updates
That the VM's public IP address will never change
That the NSG rule has been removed
questions.explain: A port being open and a service actually running and listening are two different things worth confirming separately.

questions.q: Why does the lab check /var/log/auth.log as one of the first-login tasks, before calling the VM ready?
options: To confirm the only login activity so far is the admin's own, with nothing unexpected already present
Because apt update automatically deletes that log file otherwise
Because the log file determines the VM's IP address
Auth.log is only relevant to Windows virtual machines, not Linux
questions.explain: Checking the auth log early establishes a clean baseline before the VM is handed off as genuinely ready.
